explanation_en: Derived from the verb 'bobear' (to act like a fool, to let one's guard down), the third-person past form 'bobeou' is used colloquially as a conditional conjunction meaning 'if you slip up' or 'at the slightest mistake'. It is a very native-sounding shortcut to express that a negative consequence will happen immediately if vigilance is lost.

examples.en_text: If you let your guard down on defense, the opponent scores.
examples.target_text: Bobeou na defesa, o adversário faz o gol.

examples.en_text: This sale is really fast; if you hesitate for a second, it will be out of stock.
examples.target_text: Essa promoção é muito rápida; bobeou, o estoque acaba.

examples.en_text: Don't leave your phone on the table; if you let your guard down, someone will take it.
examples.target_text: Não deixe o celular em cima da mesa; bobeou, alguém leva.

examples.en_text: At that company the pace is fast; if you slip up, someone else takes your job.
examples.target_text: Naquela empresa o ritmo é forte; bobeou, outro pega a sua vaga.

examples.en_text: Pay attention to the oven; if you lose focus for a second, the cake burns.
examples.target_text: Preste atenção no forno; bobeou, o bolo queima.

examples.en_text: The chess game was balanced, but he let his guard down and lost his queen.
examples.target_text: O jogo de xadrez estava equilibrado, mas ele bobeou e perdeu a rainha.

explanation_en: A classic, highly frequent idiomatic expression meaning 'sooner or later'. While simple, it is a crucial building block for natural-sounding Portuguese. It can be placed flexibly in a sentence, often set off by commas as a parenthetical remark.

examples.en_text: Sooner or later, he will have to talk to the boss about the raise.
examples.target_text: Mais cedo ou mais tarde, ele vai ter que falar com o chefe sobre o aumento.

examples.en_text: There's no use lying, because the truth always comes out sooner or later.
examples.target_text: Não adianta mentir, porque a verdade sempre aparece mais cedo ou mais tarde.

examples.en_text: If you don't take care of your health, sooner or later you will have problems.
examples.target_text: Se você não cuidar da saúde, mais cedo ou mais tarde vai ter problemas.

examples.en_text: Sooner or later, all companies will use artificial intelligence.
examples.target_text: Mais cedo ou mais tarde, todas as empresas vão usar inteligência artificial.

examples.en_text: You need to make a decision; sooner or later you will have to choose a path.
examples.target_text: Você precisa tomar uma decisão; mais cedo ou mais tarde terá que escolher um caminho.

examples.en_text: If you keep practicing every day, sooner or later you will speak fluently.
examples.target_text: Se você continuar praticando todos os dias, mais cedo ou mais tarde vai falar fluentemente.

explanation_en: Literally 'another conversation', this common idiom is used to indicate that a new subject or situation is completely different in scale, difficulty, or nature from what was previously discussed. It is equivalent to the English 'a whole different ballgame' and is highly useful in comparative arguments.

examples.en_text: Planning the trip was easy, but saving money for it is a whole different story.
examples.target_text: Planear a viagem foi fácil, mas poupar dinheiro para ela já é outra conversa.

examples.en_text: I don't mind helping, but doing all the work by myself is a whole different story.
examples.target_text: Eu não me importo de ajudar, mas fazer todo o trabalho sozinho já é outra conversa.

examples.en_text: If you go with him, then that's a whole different story and I'll be more relieved.
examples.target_text: Se fores com ele, aí já é outra conversa e fico mais descansado.

examples.en_text: Buying an old house is cheap, but doing the necessary renovations is a whole different story.
examples.target_text: Comprar uma casa antiga é barato, mas fazer as obras necessárias é outra conversa.

examples.en_text: She is very nice over messages, but in person it's a whole different story.
examples.target_text: Ela é muito simpática por mensagens, mas pessoalmente é outra conversa.

examples.en_text: Passing the written test is simple, but the driving exam is a whole different story.
examples.target_text: Passar no teste escrito é simples, mas o exame de condução já é outra conversa.

explanation_en: A very common colloquial expression meaning 'for real', 'seriously', or 'in earnest'. It contrasts with doing something half-heartedly or as a joke. It can modify verbs (like 'atacar pra valer') or stand alone to confirm sincerity ('É pra valer?').

examples.en_text: After the vacation, I'm going to start studying Spanish for real.
examples.target_text: Depois das férias, eu vou começar a estudar espanhol pra valer.

examples.en_text: It looks like it's going to rain for real now, we'd better get the umbrella.
examples.target_text: Parece que agora vai chover pra valer, melhor pegarmos o guarda-chuva.

examples.en_text: In the beginning it was just a joke, but now I think I'm in love for real.
examples.target_text: No começo era só uma brincadeira, mas agora eu acho que estou apaixonado pra valer.

examples.en_text: If we want to open this company, we need to dedicate ourselves for real.
examples.target_text: Se nós quisermos abrir essa empresa, precisamos nos dedicar pra valer.

examples.en_text: Yesterday's game was just a practice, but tomorrow's is for real.
examples.target_text: O jogo de ontem foi só um treino, mas o de amanhã é pra valer.

examples.en_text: She decided to change her life and started working out at the gym for real.
examples.target_text: Ela decidiu mudar de vida e começou a treinar na academia pra valer.

explanation_en: The expression 'ficar na sua' (or 'na deles' for third-person plural) means to mind one's own business, keep to oneself, or not interfere. It is highly idiomatic and common in informal spoken Portuguese. It can also mean to stay quiet or keep a low profile in a tense situation.

examples.en_text: It's better for them to mind their own business and not get involved in our conversation.
examples.target_text: É melhor eles ficarem na deles e não se meterem na nossa conversa.

examples.en_text: I decided to keep to myself to avoid any kind of argument.
examples.target_text: Eu decidi ficar na minha para evitar qualquer tipo de discussão.

examples.en_text: Pedro prefers to mind his own business during work meetings.
examples.target_text: O Pedro prefere ficar na dele durante as reuniões de trabalho.

examples.en_text: I think we should mind our own business and let them solve the problem.
examples.target_text: Acho que nós devíamos ficar na nossa e deixar que eles resolvam o problema.

examples.en_text: I asked my neighbors to mind their own business and stop asking questions.
examples.target_text: Pedi aos meus vizinhos para ficarem na deles e pararem de fazer perguntas.

examples.en_text: She is very reserved and always prefers to keep to herself.
examples.target_text: Ela é muito reservada e prefere sempre ficar na dela.

explanation_en: A standard political idiom meaning 'to take to the streets' in protest or demonstration. While it uses basic vocabulary, the combination 'ir para as ruas' (or 'tomar as ruas') is the fixed, natural way to describe public demonstrations in Portuguese. It is essential for discussing social movements and politics.

examples.en_text: The teachers decided to take to the streets to demand better working conditions.
examples.target_text: Os professores decidiram ir para as ruas para pedir melhores condições de trabalho.

examples.en_text: If the situation doesn't improve soon, the people will take to the streets to protest.
examples.target_text: Se a situação não melhorar logo, o povo vai para as ruas protestar.

examples.en_text: After the final game, thousands of fans took to the streets to celebrate the victory.
examples.target_text: Depois do jogo final, milhares de torcedores foram para as ruas comemorar a vitória.

examples.en_text: It's not enough to criticize on social media, sometimes it is necessary to take to the streets and act.
examples.target_text: Não basta criticar nas redes sociais, às vezes é preciso ir para as ruas e agir.

examples.en_text: Next Saturday, we are going to take to the streets to defend the protection of the environment.
examples.target_text: No próximo sábado, nós vamos para as ruas defender a proteção do meio ambiente.

examples.en_text: At that time, students used to take to the streets almost every week.
examples.target_text: Naquela época, os estudantes iam para as ruas quase todas as semanas.

explanation_en: 'Voltar atrás' literally means 'to go back,' but idiomatically it means to backtrack, retract a statement, or change one's mind or decision. It is highly common in both everyday conversation and political discourse when someone reverses a previous stance. It is often used with verbs like 'não ter medo de' or 'decidir.'

examples.en_text: He made a decision and now he can no longer go back on it.
examples.target_text: Ele tomou uma decisão e agora já não pode voltar atrás.

examples.en_text: We had an agreement, so you can't go back on your word.
examples.target_text: Nós tínhamos um acordo, por isso não podes voltar atrás com a tua palavra.

examples.en_text: If I could go back in time, I would do everything differently.
examples.target_text: Se eu pudesse voltar atrás no tempo, faria tudo de maneira diferente.

examples.en_text: The company decided to cancel the project and there is no way to backtrack.
examples.target_text: A empresa decidiu cancelar o projeto e não há forma de voltar atrás.

examples.en_text: She said she was going to the movies with us, but she ended up changing her mind.
examples.target_text: Ela disse que ia connosco ao cinema, mas acabou por voltar atrás.

examples.en_text: Think carefully before signing the contract, because afterwards you won't be able to back out.
examples.target_text: Pensa bem antes de assinar o contrato, porque depois não vais conseguir voltar atrás.

explanation_en: While 'vender barato' can literally mean to sell at a low price, idiomatically it often means to 'sell out' cheaply, to compromise one's values too easily, or to undervalue an asset. In political and business contexts, it is used to criticize transactions where the public or a company got a bad deal.

examples.en_text: He needed money urgently, so he sold his car very cheaply.
examples.target_text: Ele precisava de dinheiro urgente, por isso vendeu o carro muito barato.

examples.en_text: She accepted the first salary they offered; I think she undervalued herself.
examples.target_text: Ela aceitou o primeiro salário que ofereceram; acho que se vendeu barato.

examples.en_text: They wanted to get rid of the old furniture and sold everything cheaply online.
examples.target_text: Eles queriam se livrar dos móveis antigos e venderam tudo barato na internet.

examples.en_text: You are an excellent designer, you shouldn't sell yourself so cheaply to clients.
examples.target_text: Você é um excelente designer, não deveria se vender tão barato para os clientes.

examples.en_text: The real estate market was down, so he sold the apartment cheaply.
examples.target_text: O mercado imobiliário estava em baixa, então ele vendeu o apartamento barato.

examples.en_text: The inventor didn't know the value of his creation and sold the patent very cheaply.
examples.target_text: O inventor não sabia o valor da sua criação e vendeu a patente muito barato.

explanation_en: 'Vamos combinar que' is a very common colloquial transition meaning 'let's be honest,' 'let's face it,' or 'we can all agree that.' It is used to introduce a point that the speaker considers obvious or indisputable, inviting the listener to share their perspective. It is highly natural in spoken Portuguese but should be avoided in formal writing.

examples.en_text: Let's face it, yesterday's pizza was much better than today's.
examples.target_text: Vamos combinar que a pizza de ontem estava muito melhor que a de hoje.

examples.en_text: Let's agree that the boss doesn't have much patience for long meetings.
examples.target_text: Vamos combinar que o chefe não tem muita paciência para reuniões longas.

examples.en_text: Let's face it, traveling in winter is much cheaper, but the cold gets in the way a bit.
examples.target_text: Vamos combinar que viajar no inverno é bem mais barato, mas o frio atrapalha um pouco.

examples.en_text: Let's face it, learning Portuguese is not as easy as it seems.
examples.target_text: Vamos combinar que aprender português não é tão fácil quanto parece.

examples.en_text: Let's agree that this new phone is beautiful, but the price is absurd.
examples.target_text: Vamos combinar que esse celular novo é bonito, mas o preço é absurdo.

examples.en_text: Let's face it, the end of the movie was quite disappointing, don't you think?
examples.target_text: Vamos combinar que o final do filme foi bem decepcionante, não acha?

explanation_en: 'A céu aberto' is a fixed collocation meaning 'open-air' or 'outdoor.' It is commonly used to describe markets, museums, malls, or even landfills ('lixão a céu aberto'). It is a standard expression across all registers of Portuguese.

examples.en_text: In the summer, I prefer to shop at the city's open-air market.
examples.target_text: No verão, prefiro fazer compras no mercado a céu aberto da cidade.

examples.en_text: Yesterday we watched an open-air theater play in the park.
examples.target_text: Ontem assistimos a uma peça de teatro a céu aberto no parque.

examples.en_text: This small historic town is like an open-air museum.
examples.target_text: Esta pequena vila histórica é como um museu a céu aberto.

examples.en_text: During the trip, we decided to camp and sleep in the open air.
examples.target_text: Durante a viagem, decidimos acampar e dormir a céu aberto.

examples.en_text: The restaurant has a fantastic terrace for dining in the open air.
examples.target_text: O restaurante tem uma esplanada fantástica para jantar a céu aberto.

examples.en_text: The sculpture exhibition will take place outdoors in the botanical garden.
examples.target_text: A exposição de esculturas vai decorrer a céu aberto no jardim botânico.

explanation_en: 'Fazer com que' is a crucial grammatical construction meaning 'to cause to' or 'to make [someone/something do something].' It is highly important for advanced learners because it always triggers the subjunctive mood in the following verb (e.g., 'percam'). It is used in both formal and informal registers to express cause and effect.

examples.en_text: Drinking water regularly makes your skin healthier.
examples.target_text: Beber água regularmente faz com que a tua pele fique mais saudável.

examples.en_text: The heavy rain caused the flight to be canceled.
examples.target_text: A chuva forte fez com que o voo fosse cancelado.

examples.en_text: This new system makes it easier to organize daily work.
examples.target_text: Este novo sistema faz com que seja mais fácil organizar o trabalho diário.

examples.en_text: Social media makes people feel more connected.
examples.target_text: As redes sociais fazem com que as pessoas se sintam mais conectadas.

examples.en_text: Drinking coffee in the late afternoon makes me unable to sleep at night.
examples.target_text: Tomar café ao fim da tarde faz com que eu não consiga dormir à noite.

examples.en_text: The lack of organization causes the project to cost more.
examples.target_text: A falta de organização faz com que o projeto custe mais caro.

explanation_en: 'Inadvertidamente' is an advanced (B2/C1) adverb meaning 'inadvertently,' 'unintentionally,' or 'by oversight.' It is a sophisticated way to describe an action done without realizing its negative consequences. It is common in news reports, political analyses, and formal discussions.

examples.en_text: Sorry, I inadvertently deleted your message while cleaning out my inbox.
examples.target_text: Desculpe, eu apaguei a sua mensagem inadvertidamente enquanto limpava a minha caixa de entrada.

examples.en_text: During the meeting, she inadvertently revealed the plans for the surprise party.
examples.target_text: Durante a reunião, ela revelou inadvertidamente os planos para a festa surpresa.

examples.en_text: I inadvertently took the office key home.
examples.target_text: Eu levei a chave do escritório para casa inadvertidamente.

examples.en_text: We inadvertently took the longer route because the GPS wasn't working well.
examples.target_text: Nós pegamos o caminho mais longo inadvertidamente porque o GPS não estava funcionando bem.

examples.en_text: The player inadvertently touched the ball with his hand, but the referee didn't call a foul.
examples.target_text: O jogador tocou a bola com a mão inadvertidamente, mas o árbitro não marcou falta.

examples.en_text: The report contained some errors because some old data was inadvertently included.
examples.target_text: O relatório continha alguns erros porque alguns dados antigos foram incluídos inadvertidamente.
